kayitlar.yt_baslik: Did 1700s royal women really have LIVE MICE in their hair?! 🐭👑 #shorts #history #fyp
kayitlar.yt_aciklama:
In 1770s Versailles, aristocratic women wore 3-foot-tall powdered hair towers ('Pouf' hairstyles) held together with melted pig lard and pounds of wheat flour! Because these towering wigs took hours to build, they went unwashed for weeks—attracting bugs and mice at night. While the famous 'wire mouse cages' were actually 1770s newspaper satire mocking royal fashion, the pig lard pomade, diamond-encrusted bug-scratcher sticks (grattoirs), and Queen Elizabeth I's toxic white lead makeup (Venetian Ceruse) were 100% real historical facts! Would you survive 18th-century beauty standards? Comment below 👇

kayitlar.yt_aciklama:
In Ancient Rome, gladiators were the ultimate superstars. After combat in the Colosseum, attendants used a curved bronze blade called a 'strigil' to scrape the mixture of olive oil, sweat, arena dust, and dead skin off the fighters' bodies. Instead of throwing it away, they bottled the scrapings into vials (gloios) and sold them to wealthy Roman noblewomen as a luxury anti-aging face cream and aphrodisiac! Would you try Roman skincare?
